validated_results.title: Tea consumption and risk of bladder and kidney cancers in a population-based case-control study.
validated_results.reason: Population-based case-control study reporting adjusted odds ratios for usual adult tea consumption and bladder cancer risk.

extraction.population: Population-based bladder cancer cases and controls in Iowa

sample_size.excerpt: The authors examined the association between usual adult tea consumption and risk of bladder and kidney cancers in a population-based case-control study that included 1,452 bladder cancer cases, 406 kidney cancer cases, and 2,434 controls.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 1452 + 2434 = 3886

cases.excerpt: The authors examined the association between usual adult tea consumption and risk of bladder and kidney cancers in a population-based case-control study that included 1,452 bladder cancer cases, 406 kidney cancer cases, and 2,434 controls.

effect_size.excerpt: For bladder cancer, the age- and sex-adjusted odds ratios (OR) (95% confidence intervals (CI)) referent to nonusers of tea were 0.9 (0.7, 1.1) for <1.0 cup/day, 1.0 (0.8, 1.2) for 1.0-2.6 cups/day, and 0.9 (0.7, 1.1) for >2.6 cups/day (cutpoints for users based on the tertile distribution among controls). When more extreme cutpoints were used, persons who consumed >5 cups/day (>90th percentile) had a suggestive decreased risk (OR = 0.7; 95% CI 0.5, 1.0), but there was no evidence of a dose-response relation.

confidence_interval.excerpt: For bladder cancer, the age- and sex-adjusted odds ratios (OR) (95% confidence intervals (CI)) referent to nonusers of tea were 0.9 (0.7, 1.1) for <1.0 cup/day, 1.0 (0.8, 1.2) for 1.0-2.6 cups/day, and 0.9 (0.7, 1.1) for >2.6 cups/day (cutpoints for users based on the tertile distribution among controls).

gender.excerpt: the age- and sex-adjusted odds ratios

extraction.p_value_method: two-sided Wald test from effect and 95% CI on the log scale

sample_size.excerpt: We examined the relation between consumption of 22 dietary items and subsequent bladder-cancer incidence in a cohort of atomic-bomb survivors in Japan. Subjects were 38,540 people (14,873 men and 23,667 women) who responded to a mail survey carried out between 1979 and 1981 and who had no known cancer diagnosed before the start of follow-up (1 January 1980 for men, 1 February 1981 for women).

cases.excerpt: As of the end of 1993, there were 114 (83 men and 31 women) incident cases of bladder cancer among 450,326 person-years at risk.

comparison.excerpt: The consumption of the other dietary items, including meat and green tea, was not related to risk.

validated_results.title: Bladder-cancer incidence in relation to vegetable and fruit consumption: a prospective study of atomic-bomb survivors.
validated_results.reason: The cohort assessed tea (green tea) consumption frequency and subsequent bladder cancer incidence, satisfying both the exposure and the incident-cancer requirements.

extraction.comparison_type: Higher versus lower consumption frequency of green tea (no numeric estimate reported in abstract)
extraction.timing: Baseline mail survey 1979-1981, follow-up to end of 1993

sample_size.excerpt: We examined the relation between consumption of 22 dietary items and subsequent bladder-cancer incidence in a cohort of atomic-bomb survivors in Japan. Subjects were 38,540 people (14,873 men and 23,667 women) who responded to a mail survey carried out between 1979 and 1981 and who had no known cancer diagnosed before the start of follow-up (1 January 1980 for men, 1 February 1981 for women).

cases.excerpt: As of the end of 1993, there were 114 (83 men and 31 women) incident cases of bladder cancer among 450,326 person-years at risk.

comparison.excerpt: The consumption of the other dietary items, including meat and green tea, was not related to risk.

design.excerpt: a prospective study of atomic-bomb survivors

continent.excerpt: a cohort of atomic-bomb survivors in Japan

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Consumption frequencies for 22 dietary items were ascertained with pre-coded answers.
